doc.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

chapter: Biagini, Duke and the Shaw band
title: Winter road trips and playing in extreme temperatures
summary: Travelling by car with Biagini, 28 below in Binghamton, and Guadalcanal sun in the Navy.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: And when you guys went out to travel, did you mostly take two or three cars? Or was it on a bus? A train?

Cars. Yeah, it would be cars in those days, yeah. I remember with Biagini we left I think it was Erie, Pennsylvania — cold — and went to Binghamton. That’s when, I got out of that car, we checked in the hotel, and I saw this thermometer, 28 below zero. And I was dumb enough just to walk out and go the restaurant. Your ears could have dropped off I think.
Your trumpet could stick to your mouth at those temperatures.
Yeah, and I also had just the opposite of that once, in Guadalcanal, where you had to shade the mouthpiece from the sun. That was during the Navy.
